content.headline: Where science meets art.
content.subheadline: My mission is to help you achieve healthy, radiant skin — with care, expertise and the latest technology.

content.headline: A passion that began with my own skin.
content.body:
From a young age, I was fascinated by the world of skincare and beauty. My passion truly blossomed in high school when I struggled with acne. The transformation I experienced after seeing an esthetician was life-changing and planted the seed for my future career.

I was captivated by the complexities of the human body and the science behind healing. That curiosity led me towards the medical field — but it was my own battle with skin issues that redirected my path to esthetics. Transforming my skin through medical-grade treatments and skincare ignited a passion for helping others achieve the same.

After several years, I pursued further education and became licensed in esthetics, training extensively in skin types, treatments and the latest skincare technology. This blend of medical insight and esthetic expertise lets me approach beauty treatments with a unique perspective.

As a medical esthetician, I specialise in treatments that require a deeper understanding of the skin's structure and healing processes — from advanced chemical peels to microneedling. Now I am here to help you reach your skincare goals while ensuring your safety and well-being.

data.title: Facial
data.short: A deep-cleansing, circulation-boosting ritual with exfoliation, mask, moisturiser and SPF.
data.lead: A personalised facial that cleanses deeply, exfoliates away dull skin and leaves you hydrated, protected and glowing.

children.text: A facial is a skin-care treatment designed to deeply cleanse, improve circulation, exfoliate to remove dead skin cells, then mask, moisturise and protect with SPF.

We also help with common skin concerns like ageing, dry skin, acne and hyperpigmentation. Some facials incorporate oxygen, high-frequency microcurrents, dermaplaning and LED light to deliver more intense or specific results.
Facials can also be combined with chemical peels, microdermabrasion and microneedling for more comprehensive results.

data.highlights:
Deep cleanse | Lifts away impurities and prepares skin for treatment.
Exfoliation | Removes dead skin cells for a smoother surface.
Circulation boost | Encourages a healthy, rested glow.
Mask, moisturiser & SPF | Nourish first, then protect your results.

data.short: A “supercharged” Dermalogica facial that delivers actives deeper — instant glow, no downtime.
data.lead: A professional, non-invasive skin-resurfacing treatment developed by Dermalogica — instant glow with no downtime.

children.text: LuminFusion is a “supercharged” facial that uses the Dermalogica Pro Pen — a professional-grade device with stainless steel cone nanotips — to deliver active ingredients deep into the skin.
It works alongside professional-strength exfoliants and a light-energy masque, followed by red light therapy to enhance results.
This service creates an instant glow and diminishes the signs of skin ageing, all with no downtime.

Although chemical peels are used mostly on the face, they can also be used to improve the skin on your neck and hands. Sun exposure, acne or just getting older can leave your skin tone uneven, wrinkled, spotted or scarred.

data.title: Microdermabrasion
data.short: Helps thicken collagen for a younger-looking complexion.
data.lead: A resurfacing treatment that helps thicken your collagen for a younger-looking complexion.

children.text: Microdermabrasion helps to thicken your collagen, which results in a younger-looking complexion.
Collagen is a protein in your skin which is abundant when you're a child and makes skin appear taut and smooth. Collagen production declines as we age, resulting in looser, uneven skin.

data.short: Exfoliating blade treatment for a smooth, radiant surface — coming soon.
data.lead: An exfoliating blade treatment for a smooth, radiant surface. Launching soon.

children.text: Dermaplaning is a skin treatment that uses an exfoliating blade to skim dead skin cells and hair from your face. It's also called microplaning or blading.
Dermaplaning aims to make your skin's surface smooth, youthful and radiant. It's also used to remove “peach fuzz” — the short, soft hairs on your face.

data.title: Microneedling
data.short: Collagen induction therapy for scars, pores and texture — coming soon.
data.lead: Collagen induction therapy that helps skin repair itself naturally. Launching soon.

children.text: Microneedling, also called percutaneous collagen induction therapy, is performed using a handheld, drum- or pen-shaped device, electrically powered, with tiny needles that make precise, microscopic punctures in the skin.
These “micro-injuries” do not leave scars; they work by helping to stimulate the skin to repair itself naturally through a process called dermal remodelling.
Microneedling is used to treat a variety of skin conditions that cause depressions in the skin such as acne scarring, surgical scars, other scars, burns, enlarged pores, wrinkles and stretch marks.

data.title: Facial or chemical peel: which is right for you?
data.excerpt: Both refresh your skin, but they work differently. Here is how to choose — or combine them.

image.alt: Facial or chemical peel: which is right for you?

children.text: Booking your first professional treatment can feel like a menu with too many options. Two of the most popular — a facial and a chemical peel — are often confused, so here is a quick way to tell them apart.
What a facial does

A facial is designed to deeply cleanse, improve circulation, exfoliate to remove dead skin cells, then mask, moisturise and protect with SPF. It is a great fit if you are dealing with ageing, dry skin, acne or hyperpigmentation and want a complete, relaxing reset.
What a chemical peel does

A chemical peel uses a chemical solution to improve the texture and tone of your skin by removing the damaged outer layers. It can also be used on the neck and hands. If sun exposure, acne or time have left your skin uneven, spotted or scarred, a peel is a more targeted option.
The best results often come from combining treatments, not choosing just one.
Can I combine them?

Yes. Facials may be combined with chemical peels, microdermabrasion and microneedling for more comprehensive results. If you are not sure where to start, a free virtual skin consultation is the easiest way to get a personalised recommendation.

data.title: Back facials: the treatment your skin is missing
data.excerpt: Your back gets as much sun, sweat and friction as your face — yet rarely gets the same care.

image.alt: Back facials: the treatment your skin is missing

children.text: We give our faces daily attention, but the skin on our backs is often forgotten until summer or a special event. A back facial changes that.
What is a back facial?

A back treatment — most commonly called a back facial — is a professional skincare session designed to address the unique needs of the skin on your back. It follows the same core steps as a traditional facial but is tailored for the upper and mid-back.
Who is it for?
The back can be prone to acne, clogged pores, dryness, rough texture and uneven tone. If any of that sounds familiar, a 30-minute session is a simple way to deep-clean, smooth and hydrate.
Targets back acne and congestion
Smooths rough, bumpy texture
Hydrates dry, tight skin
Ready to treat your back? Book online or call us to find a time that suits you.

data.title: LED light therapy, explained simply
data.excerpt: A non-invasive treatment that uses light to support clearer, smoother-looking skin.

children.text: LED light therapy sounds high-tech, but the experience is calm and comfortable: you relax while specific wavelengths of light are directed at your skin.
How does it work?

LED light therapy is a non-invasive treatment that uses different wavelengths of infrared light to help treat various skin issues such as acne, fine lines and wound healing. Different wavelengths are chosen for different concerns.
How long does it take?
A stand-alone LED session takes about 15 minutes. It is also built into many facials, and the Pro Pen Luminfusion finishes with red light therapy to enhance results.
Fifteen minutes, no downtime, and a treatment you can add to almost any visit.
Curious whether LED is right for your skin? Book a free virtual consultation and we will talk it through.
